chapter: Central Avenue clubs, Nordskog, Sheffield and Music Town
title: How Music Town ended and the Wells Fargo building
summary: Austin McCoy was drafted, returned restless, sold out, and Spikes sold the operation to the Masonic Lodge and went into real estate.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: How long did Music Town operate?

Oh, I stayed up there till...see, Austin got drafted in the Army. He was away two, three years. And then I was there by myself, and when he come back, just like all soldiers--they wild, you know--they been cooped up so long--he didn't want to work, he come in four o'clock in the afternoon. Next day he wouldn't come at all...tryin' to, you know, I know what it is because I was in the Army myself. You try to get back to realization. So I got tired of it. One time he stay away a week. We had...I had people there waitin' for him. He wouldn't show up, and so I just sat down and said, "Austin,

if you want to buy me out, I'll sell out to you, and you operate the place, or I'll buy you out." So he sold out to me, and after I...he left, why I run it four, five months, and then I sold it out to the Lodge--you know, to the Masonic Lodge, and I went into real estate.
I see. Did you own the building there?
Just the operation of Music Town.

Wells Fargo owned the building. I'm sorry I didn't buy the building 'cause they didn't want but forty thousand dollars for the whole building. We coulda got it for maybe a thousand dollars down. They wanted to get rid of it. We didn't pay but forty dollars a month rent for the whole big hall up there, and we had six rooms. We had teachers in each room, nearly.
